messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Pager triggered: dedicated-autoscaler -> hostpool-a reporting intermittent 503s to multi-tenant routes. Threshold hit at 2026-03-15 10:12:30 UTC. Bridging in #incidents now. Paging Ben (oncall).
Ben (oncall): Got it, joining bridge. starting quick triage — any customer-facing impact confirmed?
Carla (SRE): We see elevated 503s on autoscaler v2 between 10:11–10:22. Error spike correlates with a recent autoscaler config rollout (policy change: aggressive scale-down). Full logs attached on bridge. No config rollback yet.
Ben (oncall): Noted. I'll open a short status page draft and loop CS. @Alice (CS) heads-up: some customers on Dedicated may see failed inference requests briefly.
Alice (CS): Thanks. I’ll prepare a short customer note with what we know and that we’re investigating. Need ETA for mitigations for the note.
Dave (runtime): Mitigation idea: temporarily pin hostpool-a to scale-up-min=2 and disable the recent aggressive scale-down policy. That should stop the 503 loop. Can push within ~8–10m if SRE gives the go.
Carla (SRE): +1 to pin and rollback. Root cause appears to be scaling decision thrashing: autoscaler removed GPUs during sustained short spikes because metrics window not accounting for queue length. Rolling back the policy should stabilize.
Ben (oncall): Proceed with Dave's mitigation. I’ll update the status page now.
ops-notify-bot: Status page draft posted: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/2026-03-15-dedicated-autoscaler — summary: "Investigating 503 errors affecting some Dedicated customers in hostpool-a. Mitigation in progress." (will update with timeline).
Alice (CS): Draft customer follow-up (internal) — please review/comment:

"Hi — we experienced transient 503 errors impacting some inference requests for customers using Dedicated hostpool-a between ~10:11–10:22 UTC. Our on-call team implemented a rollback of a recent autoscaler policy and pinned capacity; the service stabilized by 10:20 UTC. We will follow up with a short RCA and mitigations."

Can someone add quantification (requests impacted / customers) and a short timeline?
Carla (SRE): Adding timeline snippet — please pull into draft:
```
10:11:05 UTC - autoscaler policy rollout (aggressive scale-down) starts
10:12:30 UTC - error rate spike (503s) observed, alert triggers
10:13:00 UTC - on-call paged and bridge created
10:15:40 UTC - mitigation: pinned hostpool-a min capacity and rolled back policy
10:20:12 UTC - error rates returned to baseline
10:22:00 UTC - monitoring confirms stability; preparing incident notes
```
Ben (oncall): Quick impact quant: ~420 failed requests over 11 minutes, affecting 3 Dedicated customers (IDs masked). Alice — include that in the customer note.
Alice (CS): Updated draft with numbers. Here's the customer-facing text proposal (short):

"Hello — we recently detected and resolved a transient issue that caused a small fraction of inference requests to fail (HTTP 503) for some Dedicated customers using hostpool-a on 2026-03-15 between ~10:11–10:22 UTC. Root cause: an autoscaler configuration rollout that caused unintended rapid scale-downs under bursty short-lived load. Mitigation: we rolled back the autoscaler change and pinned capacity; normal service resumed at ~10:20 UTC. Impact: ~420 failed requests affecting 3 Dedicated accounts. Next steps: full RCA and permanent guardrails to prevent similar regressions. No customer data was exposed. We’ll share a full post-incident summary by EOD PDT."

Elaine (AM): Please add a line offering a follow-up call for affected customers and a contact email. Also mention any credits if SLA impacted.
Alice (CS): Added call offer and contact. I’ll flag potential SLA credit for review. @Ben / @Carla — will you confirm whether this qualifies for credit under our Dedicated SLA (uptime window)?
Carla (SRE): From operations view, the incident is <1 minute of service degradation per affected route when averaged across the period; billing/SLA calc team should confirm. I'll hand timeline+metrics to finance/SLA folks.
Dave (runtime): For postmortem actions I propose:
- Revert autoscaler rollout process: add canary guardrail & longer warm-up window
- Extend metrics window to include queue length to avoid scale-down during short bursts
- Add preflight check in CI for autoscaler policy diffs
- Add synthetic tests simulating bursty short requests to Dedicated hostpools

Ben (oncall): Good list. Add to action items and assign owners. We need ETA for action completion for the customer follow-up.
Alice (CS): Final internal summary ready for sign-off (will be copy/pasted to customer). Please react with :thumbsup: when you approve.

INTERNAL CUSTOMER FOLLOW-UP DRAFT:
"Hello <Customer>,

We wanted to follow up on the service disruption on 2026-03-15 that affected some inference requests on Dedicated hostpool-a. Summary:
- What happened: a recent autoscaler policy change caused unintended rapid scale-downs during short bursts, resulting in HTTP 503s.
- Impact: ~420 failed requests across 3 Dedicated accounts between ~10:11–10:22 UTC. Service returned to normal by ~10:20 UTC.
- What we did: rolled back the policy and pinned capacity to prevent further evictions; monitoring confirmed recovery.
- Next steps: permanent guardrails (canary rollout, metrics/window changes, synthetic tests). We expect a full RCA and timeline by EOD PDT today. If you'd like a call, reply and we’ll schedule."

Ben (oncall): :thumbsup:
Carla (SRE): :thumbsup:
Dave (runtime): :thumbsup:
Elaine (AM): :thumbsup: — I'll coordinate customer outreach for the 3 accounts and propose credit options if SLA applies.

incident-bot: Status page updated: "Mitigation implemented; service stabilized. RCA in progress." Link: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/2026-03-15-dedicated-autoscaler
Alice (CS): Thanks team — sending message to customers now and starting an EOD RCA draft. I’ll drop the final RCA link here once ready. Closing internal thread after one final confirmation: any outstanding asks?
Carla (SRE): I’ll open the postmortem doc and add the technical root cause/details + owners for each action item.
Ben (oncall): I'll hand off a runbook tweak to next oncall to ensure faster detection of similar thrash patterns.
Alice (CS): All good. Sending now. Will post customer receipts and update if any reply/ask comes back.
Elaine (AM): Thanks — I’ll follow up with the accounts and loop billing.
Ben (oncall): Thanks all, closing in 15. Good work.
notes: This thread contains the root message and all replies in chronological order.
Messages prefixed by sender name; includes incident bot posts, mitigation decisions, and a customer follow-up draft.
